title: Kid Rene leads the boys' band; the first parade, a carnival job for $3.50
summary: Happy's first parade was a carnival day for three and a half dollars, a good wage.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you, whatever happened to those different other guys in Richard Taylor's little band? Who was the leader of it anyway? That's the first thing. Did you have a leader in that first band?
Kid Rene was the leader of it. Kid Rene, yeah. Was it a brass band or a dance band? Brass band.

The first parade we played. The first parade I played was for the zoo. The zoo? That's the first parade. And I never forget how much we got. Three and a half a piece. And I was so glad I didn't know what to do. All day young fly playing energy. What's that? I was out there young fly playing energy. And in the evening we'd walk all day with the parade. And when we knocked off I wasn't a bit more tired than I am now. Just young and ambitious. Was that a carnival parade? Carnival day.
How long did you play for three and a half? All day. All day.

All day. That's a long job. Well that was plenty money in those days. We did that. Plenty money. You could live for a week on that. Almost. And this boy Joe, Joe, he played violinist. And afterwards he switched from violinist. And he switched from violinist.

And he switched from violinist. And he switched from violinist. And he switched from violinist. And he switched from violinist. And he was on drums. Yeah, we had a good little band. We were playing everything by hand. And we were playing it too.
